prompt_sections: #### D. Hidden Semantic Cost — 20% of quality score
#### E. Capability Efficiency — 15% of quality score
# 20. Semantic Regularity Evidence for Semantic Compression
units.goal:
Author the one canonical fragment/support record per frozen probe for the assigned language, then report metric.capability_coverage. Apply R1-R10 and the frozen support rubric exactly. evidence.canonical_fragments must contain all 44 probe IDs. Each probe record must carry level, fragment (or null for NONE), partial_reasons, none_reason, justification, and citation. These records are the sole fragment source consumed by Semantic Density, Determinacy, Locality, Hidden Cost, and Capability Efficiency.

Mechanical verification contract (mandatory for every FULL/PARTIAL probe):
- Also write evidence.canonical_verification with exactly the FULL/PARTIAL probe IDs.
- Each entry has only: entry_file, fragment_files, files, mode, run_count.
- files maps relative paths to complete UTF-8 fixture source/input files. Keep fixtures minimal. fragment_files lists, in order, the files containing the measured fragment; the canonical fragment must appear in their concatenated text unchanged except whitespace.
- The trusted runner, not you, executes the frozen language recipe. Your fixture must make the canonical_task behavior self-checking: a wrong result must make the program exit nonzero.
- For every probe listed in pre_measurement_validation.V1_fixed_stdout_oracles.by_probe, the fixture's TOTAL stdout on every successful run must equal that frozen value after leading/trailing whitespace is stripped. Do not add a second print when the canonical fragment itself already produces the required stdout. The runner compares this independently.
- entry_file is the frozen single-file entry name for the assigned language (main.qui, main.py, main.cpp, main.rs, main.go, Main.java, main.ts, main.kt, main.swift, or main.zig).
- F14.P3 and F18.P2 use the frozen multi-unit recipe. Use util.cpp for C++, util.swift for Swift, util/Util.java for Java, util.kt for Kotlin, and go.mod plus util/*.go for Go when those languages need the second unit.
- mode is "run" and run_count is 1 for ordinary probes; F19.P2 uses mode="run", run_count=20; F20.P2 uses mode="nm-add2", run_count=0.
- Do not claim build/run/nm success yourself. The validator compiles/runs after your response and rejects the work unit on any failure.

For F20.P1, work/root/f20_runtime_facts.json is trusted evidence projected from the pinned Linux runtime image before paid Semantic Compression work. For each listed language it records a successful exact-frozen-recipe build/run, no extra compiler/runtime flags, and observed stdout 3. Do not classify a listed language as NONE or cite P-b on a contrary toolchain assumption. Absence of a language from that positive-evidence file is not negative evidence.

Mechanically enforce Semantic Compression pre-measurement V3/V4 after all ten canonical fragment owners complete: every frozen probe must have at least one mechanically verified FULL implementation. V4 suspicious rows/columns, including languages with NONE on more than one third of probes, are investigated and preserved as evidence; a high NONE rate alone does not invalidate a language or block scoring unless the investigation finds an actual instrument contradiction.
